releases.summary: Nothing you can see has changed - this release only rewrites the notes developers read inside the code. Every part of the app now says which other parts depend on it, so anyone changing something can see what else moves with it. The wording was also tightened throughout, so the warnings that matter are not buried in paragraphs. Your settings, data, modules and layout are untouched.

You can install JonDash on your phone - open it in your phone browser and use Add to Home Screen on iPhone or Install app on Android, and it gets a proper icon and opens in its own window without the address bar. Every icon now comes from your own branding: the logo you uploaded, or a lettered mark from your app name. An install without a logo used to show the Next.js logo in the browser tab. Also fixes opening JonDash on a phone showing the login page until you refreshed - the browser was withholding the sign-in cookie whenever you arrived from a bookmark, another app, or a sleeping tab. Public address has moved from General to Network and HTTPS. Requesting a Lets Encrypt certificate now warns about the weekly rate limit and tells you how to rehearse it safely. Worth knowing: Android only offers to install an app over HTTPS with a certificate the phone trusts, and a self-signed one can never be enough, so use Lets Encrypt or a tunnel for that; iPhone works either way.

Beta: fixes the certificate panel saying Being served - not until you restart about a certificate that was already being served. Your HTTPS was working the whole time; JonDash was working the answer out by comparing two files instead of asking the part of itself that actually serves the certificate, and on a restart where renewal is not due that part writes nothing. It now records what it served at the moment it serves it, so one restart after updating and the line will be correct.

Beta: requesting a Lets Encrypt certificate now warns you about the weekly rate limit and tells you how to rehearse the whole process safely against their test service - a safeguard that already existed but was only mentioned in a code comment. If that test mode is switched on the page now says so plainly, because the certificate it returns is deliberately not trusted by browsers and you would otherwise think the feature was broken. Also documents that a self-signed certificate cannot be trusted by an Android phone, so a self-signed install cannot be added to an Android home screen - use Lets Encrypt or a tunnel for that.

Beta: fixes adding JonDash to an iPhone home screen giving you a shortcut rather than an app - it opened in Safari with the address bar still showing. JonDash was declaring itself installable using the modern standard wording, which iOS does not read; it now says it both ways. On Android the certificate rule is unchanged: Chrome only offers Install app over HTTPS with a certificate the phone trusts, and a self-signed one is not, so that needs your own certificate authority trusted on the phone or a real certificate.

Beta: you can install JonDash on your phone - Add to Home Screen on iPhone, Install app on Android - and it gets a proper icon and opens in its own window. Every icon now comes from your own branding: the logo you uploaded, or a lettered mark from your app name. Until now an install without a logo showed the Next.js logo in the browser tab. Also fixes opening JonDash on a phone showing the login page until you refreshed. The Public address setting has moved from General to Network and HTTPS, where the rest of the addressing lives. And for add-on authors, a class written as an example inside a code comment is no longer treated as a class you actually used - which could break the stylesheet outright.

Fixes a bug affecting every add-on. Certain styles written by a module or shared capability produced no styling at all - anything using a CSS function, such as a size that scales smoothly with the tile, a width calculated from a percentage, or a grid that fits as many columns as will go. The add-on looked correct in its own source and passed every check, and rendered wrong, with no error anywhere. JonDash was also recommending exactly the technique that was broken. Reported by the add-ons repository. Also documents, for add-on authors, that a widget can measure how wide its tile is but never how tall.

Beta: fixes a bug affecting every add-on. Certain styles written by a module or shared capability produced no styling at all - anything using a CSS function, such as a size that scales smoothly with the tile, a width calculated from a percentage, or a grid that fits as many columns as will go. The add-on looked correct in its own source and passed every check, and rendered wrong. JonDash was also recommending exactly the technique that was broken. Reported by the add-ons repository.

Fixes the buy-me-a-coffee message coming back after you dismissed it - it was remembered by your browser rather than against your account, and your phone and your PC open JonDash at different addresses, so neither knew what the other had been told. It is now remembered against you, permanently, wherever you sign in. The button also says what it does, and tells you support is still reachable from the Help and support page if you change your mind. The setup screen where you create your administrator account now states that JonDash was designed by a human and built with the assistance of AI, and links to its licence. For add-on authors: screenshots may live in a subdirectory, and the sizes JonDash resizes its own tiles at are now published so widgets from different authors adapt at the same points.

Beta: fixes the coffee message coming back after you dismissed it. It was remembered by the browser rather than against your account, and your phone and your PC open JonDash at different addresses, so neither knew what the other had been told. It is now remembered against you, so dismissing it anywhere dismisses it everywhere. The button also says what it does - Do not ask again - and pressing it now tells you that you can still support the project from the Help and support page if you change your mind. The setup screen where you create your administrator account now states plainly that JonDash was designed by a human and built with the assistance of AI, and links to its licence.

Beta: for add-on authors only - nothing changes for running JonDash. A module can put its screenshots in a subdirectory again rather than loose among its source files, and the sizes JonDash resizes its own service tiles at are now published, so widgets from different authors change shape at the same points instead of at four different ones.

The interface rework. Your dashboard now holds service tiles and add-on widgets in one grid you arrange together - drag to move, drag a corner to resize, and a tile stays where you put it instead of being packed in from the top left. Drop one on top of another and the rest shuffle out of the way. Your phone and your PC remember separate arrangements. Browsing add-ons is now a proper catalogue: click a module and it expands over the grid showing exactly what it can do, with screenshots if the author provides them, and installing is only possible from there - so a module can never be installed without its permissions having been in front of you. HTTPS no longer needs a domain name: JonDash can make its own certificate for a home network covering your LAN address, your own certificate is uploaded and checked rather than typed as a file path, and a new panel tells you when a certificate expires and whether it is actually being served. Backups now say plainly what they contain, encryption is a checkbox rather than an optional password box, and restoring reads the file as you choose it and only asks for a passphrase if it needs one. Add-ons keep their own data through a backup. JonDash also only updates when you say so - starting it will never install an update - and shut down genuinely shuts down. Plus a Help and support page, and a long list of fixes including settings that appeared to revert after saving, dropdowns that ignored the first click, and service tiles that could not be dragged.

Beta: a module can now show pictures of itself on its page before you install it, in a strip across rather than stacked down the page so the list of what it can do stays in view. No add-on publishes any yet, so you will not see a change today - JonDash had to build this side first, because add-on authors could not publish pictures into a product that ignored them. The pictures come through JonDash rather than straight from the internet, so your browser never talks to the add-on source, and JonDash checks the file type and size itself instead of taking the manifest at its word. Also removes a diagnostic line the module panel had been printing to the browser console.
Beta: the Buy me a coffee button on the help page now points at the real link instead of the placeholder it was built with. Nothing else changed.

Beta: fixes the coffee message on a phone, where its two buttons kept their full width and squeezed the sentence into a narrow strip down the side. The message and the buttons now sit on separate rows on a narrow screen. Also fixes a missing space on the help page.

Beta: there is now a Help and support page, and it sits directly below General in the settings list rather than at the bottom - help is what you reach for when something is wrong, which is the worst moment to be hunting for it. A quiet line at the foot of every screen links to it, with a little heart drawn from your own appearance settings so it takes your palette. JonDash will ask you for a coffee once, and only after you have been using it for a week - never on day one - and dismissing it means it never comes back. Nothing is ever held back from people who do not; there is no paid tier and there never will be. Every screen this release touched has also been checked at phone width.

Beta: add-ons keep their own data through a backup and restore. Until now a backup carried a module's settings but not the tables it builds for itself, so restoring left something like a health monitor configured but with none of its history. Modules and the shared capabilities behind them can now declare which of their tables belong in a backup. JonDash will not write that data into a different version of the add-on than the one that produced it - it leaves the data alone and tells you which version you would need to install to get it back, because writing old rows into a changed table corrupts an add-on rather than restoring it. Anything skipped is written to the audit log as well. Credentials stored by an add-on follow the same rule as everything else: kept in an encrypted backup, left out of a plain one.

Beta: backups are clearer about what they hold and restores are simpler. Encryption is now a checkbox, and the list of what the backup will contain grows by five lines when you tick it - your credentials, two-factor secrets, the encryption key, secret settings and icons - so it is obvious that an unencrypted backup cannot restore anyone's ability to sign in. When restoring, JonDash reads the file as you choose it, tells you whether it is encrypted and when it was made, and asks for the passphrase only if it needs one; the same happens on the first-run restore screen. Restoring is now all or nothing - the category checkboxes have gone, because the parts of a backup were never independent - and the 'type Everything' box is replaced by a plain warning that the whole server, including its network and HTTPS settings, is being replaced. The authenticator check before a restore is unchanged. Also fixed: the restore file picker used to offer every file on your computer including programs.

Beta: HTTPS without needing a domain name. JonDash can now make its own certificate for a home network - the connection is encrypted, each browser warns once until you trust it, and it covers every address this machine answers on including your LAN IP, so you don't get a second warning for the wrong reason. You pick how long it lasts, from 30 days to 7 years. If you have your own certificate you now upload it instead of typing a file path: the pair is checked before anything is saved, so a mismatched key is caught immediately rather than at the next restart, and the files are copied into JonDash so moving the originals can't break HTTPS later. A new panel tells you who your certificate was issued to and by, when it expires, which addresses it covers, and whether it is actually being served yet. And a Let's Encrypt certificate can be requested on the spot rather than waiting for a restart, with Let's Encrypt's own explanation shown if it refuses.

Beta: the module panel in Browse genuinely expands out of the card you clicked now - the previous two betas said so and neither did it. The animation had been running for a fifth of a millisecond because of how the timing was read from your interface style. The panel also falls back to a plain animation if anything goes wrong with the clever one, so it can never simply appear again. Windows XP and Terminal still open instantly, and reduced motion still turns everything off.

Beta: the module panel in Browse now genuinely expands out of the card you clicked, instead of appearing fully formed. The animation was there in beta.18 but started a fraction after the browser had already drawn the finished panel, so there was nothing left to watch. Each interface style keeps its own timing - Crystal is unhurried, Brutalist snaps through, and Windows XP and Terminal do not animate at all, because a window in those was either up or it wasn't. If you have asked your system for reduced motion, nothing animates on any style.

Beta: clicking a module in Browse now expands it over the catalogue instead of taking you to another page - it grows out of the card you clicked, and the grid stays behind it on the same page and scroll position, so closing it puts you right back where you were. Escape, Back, clicking outside and the X all close it, and the address still names the module so links and reloads still open the full page. Modules you already have now carry a green tick, and a card tells you if the version you have is older than the published one. Two fixes: a queued batch of installs no longer offers to install the same modules again after the restart, and the startup window no longer prints a garbled character where a dash should be.

Beta: a proper module catalogue. Browse now shows modules three across, each with a short summary and a chip telling you roughly how much access it wants, and you pick how many to show per page. Clicking one opens its own page, where you can read exactly what it can do before deciding - and that is now the only place you can install from, so a module can never be installed without its permissions having been in front of you. You can still queue several and install them together as one restart. The Addons page has tidied up too: Import is a button in the top row instead of a large panel at the bottom, and there is a new 'Design your own module' option linking the authoring guide and a template you can copy. The authoring guide itself has been brought up to date with the new dashboard grid.

Beta: dropping a tile onto another one now moves the others out of the way instead of refusing. Only the tiles actually in the way shift, each to the nearest free space, so any gaps you have deliberately left elsewhere stay exactly as they are - and the tile you are holding always lands where you put it. The board rearranges when you pause over a spot or when you let go, rather than constantly while you move, which stops the shuffling looking frantic and gives you a preview: hover somewhere for a moment and you can see what dropping there would do. Dropping a tile also lands cleanly now instead of sliding into place from where you were holding it.

Beta: a tidier arrange mode. The little arrow buttons and Reset have gone from each tile while you are arranging - only the size badge stays. The arrows moved a tile one square at a time, which is a lot of clicking now that you can simply drag a tile wherever you want it. Worth knowing: moving a tile is now done by dragging only. Resizing still works from the keyboard using the corner handle.

Beta: JonDash only updates when you say so. Starting the dashboard will never install an update any more - it just tells you one is available. Updates now happen on the schedule you set, or when you press the button in Admin - Updates, and nothing else. Scheduled updates cover JonDash itself as well as your add-ons, and a version that previously failed is never retried on its own. Shut down now genuinely shuts down: it used to be possible for a restart, and even an update, to happen anyway. On the dashboard, dragging a tile follows your cursor properly instead of moving roughly twice as far, small tiles no longer have their name cut off (the icon shrinks, and on a very small tile the name steps aside), and resizing a tile shows the new size straight away.

Beta: arrange your dashboard however you like. A tile's position is now an actual place on the grid rather than a spot in a queue, so you can put one icon at the top and another at the bottom with empty space between them, and it stays that way. Dragging is much calmer too - while you move something, nothing else on the dashboard shifts around, and the layout only changes when you let go. Two things that were broken are fixed: service tiles could not be dragged at all (only module widgets could), and hovering over a service cut off the top of its card. The arrange arrows now move an item up and down as well as left and right, which is the only way to rearrange without a mouse. Your existing dashboard is untouched by the upgrade - it keeps the arrangement it already had until you move something.

Beta: three fixes from testing. Dropdowns change on the first attempt - a setting like Session length sometimes needed two or three goes before it would move, and now responds immediately. Dragging a large module widget around the dashboard no longer flings the smaller tiles about: a tile only swaps places once you are properly over it rather than as soon as you touch its edge, and nothing shoots off the screen and back. And there is now a 'back to top' button in the bottom-right corner once you have scrolled down a page, which matters most on a phone, where arranging the dashboard used to leave you with no way back up to the Done arranging button.

Beta: settings that stay saved, and dragging that feels like dragging. If you changed a setting and watched the control snap back the moment you pressed Save, that is fixed - and the setting had been saving correctly all along, it was only the screen that went back to the old value. Every settings screen now tells you when you have unsaved changes, and the Save button only lights up when there is something to save. Rearranging your dashboard no longer drags a grey box around: the tile follows your finger or your cursor and everything else moves out of the way as you go, on a phone as well as a desktop. Tiles can now be made three times smaller than before, right down to a small square, and there is no longer a limit on how tall you can make one. A service you have just added shows up on your dashboard straight away instead of after a reload, and module widgets lift on hover while you are arranging, the same way service tiles already did.

Beta: JonDash's email now looks like JonDash. The test email arrives properly laid out, carrying your instance's name and your chosen accent colour, rather than as a bare block of text. It works for every one of the seven styles and twenty colour choices without a separate design for each, because the colours are worked out when the message is sent. The background stays light whatever palette you use - a fair number of mail apps override a dark background and leave the light text sitting on it, which produces a message you cannot read, and that is worse than one that looks plain. Every message still carries a plain-text version built from the same content, for anyone reading mail without formatting. This first pass covers JonDash's own test email; the rest of its messages, and the ability for add-ons to send through the same design, follow in a later beta.

Beta: the Email page is clearer. The provider preset dropdown is gone - it filled in a server address and port you then had to understand anyway, and said nothing about the thing people actually get stuck on, which is that Gmail and Outlook want a special app password rather than your normal one, and that Microsoft 365 turns SMTP off per mailbox until you turn it on. In its place, links at the foot of the page to each provider's own instructions - which stay correct when a provider changes a hostname, where anything copied into JonDash would quietly go stale. The password field is now just called Password, because that is what it is for a self-hosted mail server, and it now says plainly that it is stored encrypted along with the rest of your mail settings - which was already true and simply never shown.

Beta fixes from testing. Dashboard tiles are now SQUARE: one grid unit is the same size across as it is down, so a 2x2 is genuinely a square and you can make anything the shape you want by combining them. Before, the rows were a fixed height while the columns stretched with the window, so the same setting looked like a wide letterbox on one screen and a tall box on another. Widgets no longer get a scrollbar when their contents do not fit - anything too big for its box is simply cut off, and it is the add-on's job to lay itself out for the space it has been given. Fixed: choosing a new Session length appeared to do nothing. It saved correctly every time, but the box on screen snapped back to the old value until you reloaded the page, which looked exactly like a failed save. It now shows what you picked, tells you when there is an unsaved change, and the Save button stays greyed out until there is something to save. Also added 365 days as the longest Session length, matching the absolute limit.

Beta: the update list now shows what will actually happen, and you can stop JonDash opening a browser when it starts. On Admin > Updates everything waiting is ticked when the page loads, and the button says how many are ticked. Before, the boxes all appeared UNTICKED and the button said 'Update all' - so the page showed you five things not selected above a button that would update all five, which reasonably reads as being unable to choose between JonDash and your add-ons. You always could; the screen never showed it. Untick JonDash and only the add-ons update, untick everything and the button greys out rather than quietly doing the lot. Separately: JonDash opens a browser the first time it starts on a machine, which is unwanted on a server you reach from somewhere else. There is now a switch for it under Admin > Server power. For a machine you cannot see the screen of at all, set the JONDASH_NO_BROWSER environment variable instead - a switch inside JonDash is no help until you can already reach JonDash.

Beta: one setting for how long you stay signed in, instead of two that overlapped. There used to be a 'Session lifetime' in days and an 'Idle timeout' in minutes, and the way they interacted was genuinely confusing - switching the idle one off quietly made the lifetime the only thing ending a session, and the help text under it referred to a seven-day lifetime that stopped being true the moment you changed the setting above it. There is now a single 'Session length': how long you stay signed in without using JonDash. Keep using it and you stay signed in; leave it longer than that and you sign in again. It is a list of sensible choices from one hour to ninety days rather than a box of minutes, because a box that has to hold both 'two hours' and 'thirty days' tells you nothing. Nothing about your current setting changes on update: if you had an idle timeout it is kept exactly, and if you had it switched off then your old lifetime becomes the new window, so no session gets shorter or longer than it was. The absolute limit has not gone away - it is now fixed at 365 days and stated on the page, so a sign-in still cannot last forever even if it is used every single day, which is what stops a stolen session being kept alive indefinitely.

Beta: one dashboard, arranged how you like it, and it finally uses your whole screen. Your service tiles and your module widgets used to be two separate grids that could not be mixed - tiles on top, modules underneath, and no way to put a module between two tiles. They are now a single grid you arrange together: press Arrange, move anything anywhere, resize it, done. Your existing arrangement is kept, and tiles and widgets come out the size they were, so nothing is shuffled by the change itself. The dashboard also no longer sits in a narrow column in the middle of a wide monitor - it stretches to the room available, while pages that are mostly text keep their comfortable reading width, because a settings form two thousand pixels wide would be worse than the problem. And your phone now remembers its own arrangement, separate from your computer's. Rearranging on a small screen no longer reorders your desktop, and the other way round. Both start out identical, so nothing changes until you deliberately arrange one of them differently. Anything that does not fit its box scrolls inside itself rather than pushing the rest of the dashboard around.

Beta fix: resizing one dashboard widget no longer changes the size of another. Making a widget taller could nudge an unrelated one next to it slightly smaller, which was introduced by the previous beta's fix for the Height setting. The rows were allowed to grow to fit whatever was in them, and a widget covering several rows spreads its contents across all of them - so changing one widget quietly re-sized rows it shared with its neighbour, and the neighbour moved. Rows are now a fixed height, so making something taller adds exactly that much and nothing else on the dashboard shifts. Widgets sharing a row are now genuinely the same height, which is what was wanted in the first place. A widget with more content than fits its box now scrolls inside itself rather than stretching the dashboard around it.

Beta: nothing changes in the app - this fixes a test that could fail for reasons that had nothing to do with JonDash. Several of the checks that verify the Windows permission tool run it for real and wait on Windows itself to answer, and Windows can take longer than the test was allowed on a cold build machine. One of those checks was given more time when it first went red; the others were left as they were, so today a different one failed the same way while the identical code had passed an hour earlier. They now all share one realistic time limit, so a genuinely stuck test still fails and a slow machine no longer does. If you are on 1.8.0-beta.2 the app itself is unchanged.

Beta: two controls that looked like they worked and did not, plus clearer names in the Security menu. Permissions is now Addon Permissions, because it is entirely about what an ADD-ON may do - and it sat one line above Access Roles, which is about what a PERSON may do. Access Roles is now Admin Roles and has moved directly under Service Groups, since both answer the same question about a person: one for services, one for admin powers. Fixed, and this is the important one: a permission you turned OFF on the Addon Permissions page came back on its own. Switching an add-on off and on again was enough, and so was updating it - the full set it originally asked for was written back every time, while the page carried on showing the capability as off. A revocation that any routine action quietly undoes is worse than no switch at all. Turning something off now stays off: an add-on keeps exactly what you have left it, loses anything its new version no longer asks for, and gains nothing without the approval screen asking you first. Fixed: admin roles could be assigned to an administrator, where they did nothing whatsoever. The tick-boxes saved, stayed ticked and had no effect, because an administrator already holds every capability - so anyone who unticked things believing they had limited that account had not. Those tick-boxes are replaced with a plain statement, for administrators and for service accounts. Anything already assigned is kept rather than thrown away, so changing the account back to a normal user restores exactly what it had. Also corrected a help note under Idle timeout that claimed a session lasts 'its full 7-day lifetime' - it stopped being true the moment anyone changed the setting above it, and read as a fact rather than a stale default.

Beta: the dashboard is cheaper to draw, and arranging it is now something you turn on. Two faults were making every page more expensive to scroll than it needed to be, and both were invisible because nothing looked wrong. Every panel carried a backdrop blur even in the styles that have no blur at all - and a blur of zero is not free, it still makes the browser take a full pass over everything behind that panel. On a dashboard of 36 tiles that was 37 separate layers covering the whole screen, for no visible difference whatsoever. The page content also kept a leftover transform forever after its fade-in had finished, which kept the entire page on its own layer permanently. Both are gone, and the styles that genuinely use frosted glass - Crystal and Aero - look exactly as they did. Arranging your widgets is now a mode: press Arrange, move and resize, press Done. Previously the controls appeared when you hovered over a widget, which does not work on a touch screen at all, and they sat exactly where a module puts its own Open button so they took the click instead of it. The rest of the time a widget is simply something you click to open. In Arrange mode each widget gets move buttons, a size readout and a corner you can drag to resize; the arrow keys work on that corner too, so it is not mouse-only. Fixed: the widget Height setting did nothing whatsoever. The grid had no row height for a taller widget to span, so choosing Height 2 saved your choice, redrew the page and changed nothing at all. Widgets sharing a row are also a consistent height now, and a short widget fills the space it was given instead of leaving a gap under it.

Service accounts - an identity for an add-on, that nobody can ever sign in as. Create one under Users by picking 'Service account' as the type, alongside creating a person. It can hold permissions and appears in the audit log under its own name, but it has no password, no authenticator, no recovery codes and no setup link, and none of those can be added to it later. Previously an assistant had to borrow a real person's account, which meant the audit log blamed you for what it did and revoking the assistant meant locking yourself out; those are now separate things. It cannot be turned into a login: resetting access, completing a setup link and signing in are all refused, and a sign-in attempt answers exactly like an unknown address so nobody can discover one exists by trying. It never counts as your last administrator either - delete every real admin and the first-run recovery screen still appears, so an install cannot end up locked away behind an account nobody can use. Its page shows when it was last used and by which add-on, and says plainly that the key lives in the add-on rather than in JonDash, which never sees it and cannot re-issue it. Disabling the account cuts off every add-on at once. Also fixed: switching an add-on off now actually stops the shared component it uses, which mattered for the first one that holds a connection open.

Beta fix: switching an add-on off now actually stops the shared component it uses. Until now those components started whenever they were installed, whether or not any add-on using them was switched on. For almost every one that made no difference, because they sit idle until an add-on calls them - but it mattered for the first one that holds a connection open, where turning the add-on off left the connection listening and nothing on screen said so. You could reasonably believe you had closed it when you had not. Found by the add-ons author while building it; their own component was already patched, and this fixes it for every add-on including ones not written yet, so nobody has to rediscover it. Database upgrades still run for everything installed whether switched on or not, so turning an add-on back on can never meet an out-of-date layout.

Beta: creating an account is now one form with a Type of Person or Service account, instead of two separate cards, and the fields change to suit what you are making - a person has an email, a service account has a name and its handle is generated for it. Also removed the 'credential type' choice when creating a service account. It offered API key or username and password, and the second could never be true: a service account has no password, no add-on can give it one, and anything that signed in that way would be a login, which is the one thing the feature exists to prevent. The credential is always issued and held by the add-on, so labelling the account described the add-on's plumbing rather than the account and invited exactly that confusion. The account's page still shows what actually matters - when it was last used and by which add-on.

Beta: a service account now tells you what it is for. The first version created an account you could not sign in as and then showed you nothing about it, which made it indistinguishable from one created by mistake and forgotten. Its page now has a 'How this account is used' panel showing what kind of credential it is for, when it was last used and which add-on used it - and an account nothing has touched says so plainly. It is now explicit, both when you create one and on its page, that the key lives in the add-on rather than in JonDash: JonDash never sees it, cannot show it to you and cannot re-issue it, so to see, re-issue or revoke a key you go to that add-on's own settings page, named for you where we know which add-on it is. You can also record what kind of credential an account is for when creating it. Disable now says what it actually does - 'cuts off every add-on' - because that single action stops every add-on using the identity, since they re-check it on every request and you never have to hunt down individual keys. Sections that cannot apply to a service account are gone: no Service Groups, no Personal services, no Reset access. A person's account is unchanged.

Beta: service accounts. You can now create an identity for an add-on to act as, alongside creating a person, and nobody can ever sign in as it - no password, no authenticator, no recovery codes, no setup link, and none of those can be added later. Until now an assistant had to borrow a real person's account, which meant the audit log blamed you for what it did and revoking the assistant meant locking yourself out; those are now separate things. It cannot be turned into a login: resetting access, completing a setup link and signing in are all refused, and a sign-in attempt answers exactly like an unknown address so nobody can discover one exists by trying. It also never counts as your last administrator - delete every real admin and the first-run recovery screen still appears, so an install cannot end up locked away behind an account nobody can use. Disable or delete one in a single action and any add-on holding a key for it drops that key.

A new Permissions page, and Modules and Helpers merged into one Addons section. Permissions answers two questions on one screen - what a single addon is allowed to do, and which addons can do a given thing. The second is the one that catches trouble ('what can reach my files?') and you could not work it out before without opening every addon in turn. Each permission is a switch you can turn off, and turning one off takes effect immediately - the addon keeps working, that one capability stops answering. Where a permission is limited to a list - which services, which folders - that list now sits on the same screen as the switch, because a limit you have to go and find is how the recent security problems happened. You pick entries from a browsable list rather than typing names exactly right, and a per-entry setting like 'this one may act without asking me' sits on the entry it applies to. Where an addon can be given access to everything, that is a choice rather than a hidden default: turning it on reveals a second switch, 'exclude JonDash's own data', which starts on and covers the encryption key protecting your passwords and two-factor secrets, the database, and the files JonDash uses to ask Windows for administrator rights. Turning that one off is the step that asks you to confirm, because it is the direction that gives more away. Helpers are no longer a separate menu item: they were never separately installable, so a second entry implied a control that did not exist. They appear as Shared capabilities on the Addons page.

Beta: everything in 1.7.2-beta.1, plus a choice where an addon is given access to everything. Turning on 'allow everything' for something like file access now reveals a second switch underneath it - 'exclude JonDash's own data' - which starts on. That covers the encryption key that protects your passwords and two-factor secrets, the database, and the files JonDash uses to ask Windows for administrator rights. Leaving it on means everything except those; turning it off means genuinely everything, and it asks you to confirm before it will, because that is the direction that gives more away. The point is that the sentence next to the switch is true whichever way you set it - JonDash is not quietly excluding things you were told it would reach, and not quietly including the ones that matter most.

Beta: a new Permissions page, and Modules and Helpers merged into one Addons section. Permissions answers two questions on one screen - what a single addon is allowed to do, and which addons can do a given thing. The second is the one that catches trouble ('what can reach my files?') and you could not work it out before without opening every addon in turn. Each permission is a switch you can turn off, and turning one off takes effect immediately - the addon keeps working, that one capability stops answering. Where a permission is limited to a list - which services, which folders - that list now sits on the same screen as the switch rather than somewhere else, because a limit you have to go and find is how the recent security problems happened. You pick entries from a browsable list rather than typing names exactly right, and where an addon offers a per-entry setting - this one may act without asking me each time - that sits on the entry it applies to. Helpers are no longer a separate menu item: they were never separately installable, so a second entry implied a control that did not exist. They appear as Shared capabilities on the Addons page, in their own list rather than mixed in with the addons you can install and remove.

Groundwork. Nothing here changes JonDash on its own - it is the foundation that lets add-ons do things JonDash itself is not allowed to do, like restarting a Windows service or installing software. The add-ons that use it are being built separately. Add-ons can control Windows services with your approval given once: you approve one service at a time - may JonDash restart Plex? - and after that it can do that one thing without asking again. What gets saved names one service and one action and cannot be edited into something else afterwards; you can see and remove them yourself in Windows Task Scheduler under a JonDash folder, showing who added each one and when. Nothing runs in the background waiting for orders and nothing keeps administrator rights between uses. Add-ons can also install software for you, which asks every single time because what is being installed changes each time - read the add-on's screen rather than the Windows prompt, since Windows can only say that JonDash wants administrator rights, not what is being installed. Add-ons can ask you something when you remove them, answered on the confirmation screen, with every question saying who is asking. Fixed: add-ons that need setting up are now configured in JonDash rather than through a module, closing a hole where a module could edit the list of what it was allowed to do; and an action could previously happen without being recorded if the log entry could not be written.

Beta: add-ons that need setting up now have a place in JonDash to do it, on Admin > Helpers, rather than through whichever module happens to use them. This closes a real hole. An add-on that keeps an admin-approved list - say, which Windows services JonDash may restart - had nowhere to edit that list except inside a module, so the module could edit it. It could show you a button saying 'Add Plex' and actually add something else entirely, and the Windows prompt names JonDash rather than the service, so nothing on screen would have shown you the difference. The list that limits what a module can do is no longer editable by a module: it is edited on a JonDash admin page, and JonDash checks you are an administrator before the add-on sees anything. Every change is recorded, including ones that are refused.

Beta: on the uninstall screen, the name of whatever is asking a question now appears ABOVE the question rather than below it. JonDash cannot control the wording a module chooses, so a module could word its question to look as though it came from something else - and with the real name underneath, you would read the claim before the correction. Putting it first means you see who is asking before you see what they are asking. Same information, and on a screen about permissions the order is the point.

Beta: add-ons can now ask you something when you remove them, on the confirmation screen, so you answer while you are still there rather than the add-on guessing. The case it was built for is 'also remove Docker Desktop?' when the Docker module goes - removing it automatically would be wrong since it is your software and probably in use, but quietly leaving it behind is not right either. Every question says who asked it, so a module's wording is never mistaken for JonDash's. A module you installed cannot pre-tick anything on a screen whose job is confirming something you cannot undo; add-ons that ship with JonDash may set a default. Ten questions maximum, text only, no formatting or links. And a broken module cannot make itself unremovable - if asking fails or hangs you get the uninstall without its questions rather than no uninstall at all.

Beta: groundwork for add-ons that can install software for you - Docker, for instance, if you do not already have it. Unlike the service permissions added earlier, an install asks your approval every single time, because the thing being installed changes each time and there is nothing fixed to approve once. Windows will only tell you that JonDash is asking for administrator rights, not what it wants to install, so the add-on's own screen has to name the package and you should read it. Only installing and removing a named package from the official Windows package source is possible - there is deliberately no way to pass extra options to an installer, install from a file, or pick an old version, since any of those would amount to running anything at all as an administrator. Nothing to use it with yet; the Docker add-on is being built separately.

Beta: the cleanup added in the previous build could not actually work. Removing a permission needs your approval, and approving takes as long as it takes you to read the prompt - but the cleanup was cut off after five seconds. So the prompt was abandoned underneath you and the permission survived, which was the whole thing it was meant to prevent. Add-ons that need to ask you something during removal now get the time to do it. This is safe to wait on because it only happens while you are sat there having just clicked uninstall.

Beta: closes the last way a permission could be left behind. Add-ons that need special access are removed automatically once no module uses them - but until now they had no chance to tidy up first, so anything they had registered with Windows could outlive them. They can now do that cleanup on removal. If the cleanup fails or takes too long the add-on is still removed and the problem is recorded, so nothing can get stuck half-removed.

Beta: fixes a defect found while testing the service-permission feature by hand. Adding a permission worked, but JonDash was told nothing about what it had just created - the list of new entries came back empty, because the part that runs with administrator rights reports to its own hidden window. It now reads the result back from Windows itself, which is the authoritative answer anyway. The obvious shortcut - handing the elevated part a file to write its results into - was deliberately avoided, because JonDash chooses that location without administrator rights and it would have amounted to writing any file anywhere as an administrator, which is exactly what this design exists to prevent. Also in this release: the manual test itself, which confirmed the whole model works. Adding a permission needs your approval once; using it needs none; and from an ordinary account the permission cannot be rewritten, disabled or deleted - Windows refuses all three.

Beta: fixes to the service-permission groundwork, all found by the add-ons session, which now has the feature working end to end - one approval when a service is added, then start and stop with no further prompts. Fixed: an action could happen without being recorded. If the log entry could not be written - most easily when it named a user account that no longer exists - the entry was quietly dropped and the action went ahead anyway, which is the one thing an audit log exists to prevent. The entry is now always written; if we cannot tell who asked, it is recorded as unattributed and says so, and granting a new permission is refused outright if it cannot be recorded at all. Fixed: saving the same permission twice created a duplicate, and because removal matches by name, deleting one wiped both - two differently-named entries could also end up sharing a single permission, so removing one silently revoked the other. Re-saving now updates the existing entry and a genuine name clash is refused with an explanation. Fixed: a slow decision looked like a breakage - you now get ten minutes to answer the Windows prompt instead of two, and taking too long is reported as timed out rather than failed. Added: using a permission is now logged, not just granting or removing one.

Beta: groundwork for letting add-ons control Windows services (restarting Plex, say) without asking your permission every single time. Restarting a service needs administrator rights, which JonDash does not have, so this adds a small program - jondash-grant.exe - that records your decision with Windows once. You approve one service at a time, answering the question you actually care about: may JonDash restart Plex? After that it can do that one thing and nothing else. What gets saved is a fixed instruction naming one service and one action; it cannot be edited into something else later, and it cannot be handed different orders when it runs. Everything is visible in Windows' own Task Scheduler under a JonDash folder, showing who added it and when, and you can delete one there or from JonDash. Removing a module, the add-on, or JonDash itself takes its permissions with it. Nothing runs in the background waiting for orders and nothing keeps administrator rights between uses. There is nothing to use it with yet - the add-on that will is being built separately, so this release only lays the foundation. Windows only for now.

Make it yours. Choose how the whole interface looks: seven styles, each with its own palettes - twenty combinations - under Admin > Settings > Appearance. Modern (Indigo/Nord/Solarized), Crystal (Aurora/Neon), Aero (Sky/Twilight/Slate), XP (Luna Blue/Olive Green/Silver), Terminal (Phosphor Green/Amber/Cyan), Brutalist (Yellow/Cyan/Mono) and Paper (Newsprint/Sepia/Ink). Each style also moves the way it should - XP snaps and shows the era's marching-blocks progress bar, Crystal takes its time, Terminal blinks a block cursor - and your system's reduced-motion setting is respected. Installed modules follow the style too. You can also make it your own instance: change the app name, upload a logo and pick an accent, all of which appear in the header, the browser tab and its icon, and on the sign-in page. Rearrange your dashboard by dragging widgets, with sizing and position now behind a small edit icon. Phones and tablets get a proper slide-out admin menu. Update all now updates JonDash itself as well as your add-ons, in that order. Fixed: the official JonDash module source can no longer be removed (disabling is still fine), and applying an update no longer signs everyone out - that affected 1.6.2.

Beta: Aero and Paper are now styles of their own - 7 styles, 20 palettes. Both had been offered as a colour of another style, but neither was really a colour: Aero was changing the corner radius, the blur and the typeface, and Paper the shadows and radius. As proper styles they get to be themselves. Aero now frames every panel the way Windows 7 did, with a highlight along the top and gradient buttons, in Sky, Twilight or Slate. Paper is ink on stock - a serif face, hairline rules and no shadows anywhere - in Newsprint, Sepia or Ink. If you were already using either, you simply keep using it: your setting moves with the style rather than falling back to something you didn't choose. Crystal now offers Aurora and Neon; Modern offers Indigo, Nord and Solarized.

Beta: styles now have a colour choice - 5 styles, 16 palettes. Several styles turned out to be the same shape in different colours, so the two are now separate: a style is the structure (corners, borders, shadows, glass, title bars, type) and a palette is the colour that fills it. Pick Modern then Indigo, Nord, Solarized or Paper; XP then Luna Blue, Olive Green or Silver; Crystal offers Aurora, Neon and Aero; Terminal offers Phosphor Green, Amber and Cyan; Brutalist offers Yellow, Cyan and Mono. The picker is two levels - compact style tiles grouped by family, then that style's palettes. Each style also now moves the way it should: XP no longer transitions at all and shows the era's marching-blocks progress bar instead of a spinner, Crystal is slower and eases, Terminal doesn't move and blinks a block cursor, Brutalist jumps in visible steps. Reduced-motion settings are respected. Appearance is now its own settings section, separate from Branding. Fixed: the official JonDash module source can no longer be removed - disabling it is still fine, but removing it left no way to install official modules.

Beta: the accent colour is now a Modern-style option, shown under the style you have chosen. It only ever affected Modern - XP and Crystal carry their own palettes as part of their look - but it was offered as a general setting, so on those styles it silently did nothing. Each style now has its own settings block: Modern's holds the accent, and XP and Crystal say plainly that they have no options of their own. Every colour in the app now comes from the style too - a sweep found status colours (update criticality, warnings, the success tick, danger text) hardcoded in a dozen places where no style could reach them, and all 15 pages were then checked under XP with nothing left painted in the old palette. Also fixed: a module with a settings panel but no settings list showed a button labelled 'Channel', pointing at a page that no longer manages channels and giving no obvious way into its settings - it now reads Settings whenever a module has any, and Manage otherwise.

Beta: fixes updating signing you out. Applying an update looked fine and then logged everyone out the moment you moved to a page you had not opened yet. JonDash decides 'does this restart keep people signed in?' as it starts, but that decision was being re-made later - by which time the marker saying this was a deliberate restart had already been tidied away, so it concluded nobody should stay signed in. The decision is now made once per start and everything else follows it. This affected 1.6.2 onwards, so update if you are on one of those. Also: your branding now shows on the sign-in page, which was still showing JonDash and the default mark to anyone signing in - the one screen where a renamed instance most needs to look like itself. Your name, logo and accent colour all appear there now.

Beta: choose how JonDash looks. The interface now comes in styles and you pick one under Admin > Settings > Branding - Modern (the standard look, following your system light/dark setting), XP (bevelled buttons, tan panels, a bright blue desktop and Tahoma - one committed look that ignores dark mode on purpose), and Crystal (translucent frosted-glass panels over a soft gradient, following light/dark). More will follow. Your accent colour and logo carry across every style: the style is the chrome and your branding sits on top of it. Installed modules are restyled along with everything else without their authors doing anything, because a style only redefines the shared design tokens and never targets one page or component. The rules every style must follow - no layout changes, no shrinking of tap targets, a visible keyboard focus ring and a contrast floor - are written down in docs/STYLES.md.

Beta: UI rework phase 4 - your own logo, and a more legible interface. You can now upload a logo under Admin > Settings > Branding (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF up to 2 MB); it replaces the square lettermark in every header and is used as the browser-tab icon, and removing it brings the lettermark back. Uploads are resized and re-saved as PNGs so nothing hidden inside a file is kept, and SVGs are refused. Keyboard focus is visible again - buttons, links and inputs show a clear focus ring when you tab to them, where the custom styling previously left almost no indication of where you were. Buttons also carry a subtle shadow in your own accent colour rather than a fixed one. Fixed: changing the logo now takes effect immediately instead of up to 30 seconds later.

Beta: 'Update all' now updates JonDash as well as your add-ons. It previously skipped JonDash itself and updated only modules and helpers, so the one button that reads like 'update everything' left the app on its old version. One button now runs the whole thing in the right order - JonDash first, then add-ons, then done - because a new module version often needs the newer JonDash, never the other way round. JonDash updates and restarts, then you see 'JonDash is updated - updating your add-ons next', then the finished screen once they are done; stay on the page and it runs to the end by itself. If the add-ons cannot be updated it says so and stops, naming the reason, confirming JonDash itself is fine and pointing you at Admin > Updates - it will not retry in a loop. You can also tick JonDash and add-ons together in the list now; they used to be mutually exclusive.

Beta: UI rework phase 3 - arrange your dashboard by dragging. Grab a module widget by the grip in its corner and drop it anywhere in the grid; it moves as you drop it and the new arrangement is remembered for you alone, without affecting anyone else's dashboard. The old 'Customise' link is now a small edit (pencil) icon, with width, height, position and Reset to default tucked inside it, so the dashboard stays clean until you actually want to change something - both the grip and the pencil stay out of sight until you hover over a widget. You can still move widgets without dragging: the edit popover keeps the arrow position buttons, which work with a keyboard and on touch, where dragging doesn't.

Beta: UI rework phase 2 - make it yours. You can now rename the app under Admin > Settings > Branding: the name shows in the header and the browser tab, and the square mark takes its first letter. New authenticator enrolments use the new name, while entries already in your authenticator keep the old name and keep working, because the underlying secret never changes. You can also set your own accent colour - a hex colour of your choice replaces the default purple on buttons, links and highlights in both light and dark mode, and text on the accent switches between black and white automatically so it stays readable whatever you pick; leave it blank for the default. Also: the section headings in the Settings navigation (Server settings, Security) now sit on a divider and are smaller, bolder and wider-spaced, so they read as headings rather than as options you can tap - on both the mobile slide-out and the desktop sidebar.

Beta: UI rework, phase 1 of several - the look and layout are being refreshed in stages, and nothing about your services or data changes. This first beta reworks the mobile admin navigation: on a phone, the admin Menu dropdown is replaced by a hamburger button that slides the full Settings navigation out from the left, grouped exactly like the desktop sidebar. Pick a section and it navigates and closes itself; tap outside or the close icon to dismiss. The desktop sidebar is unchanged.

Everything since 1.6.0 in one release - security hardening plus restarts that no longer sign you out. Most of this is behind the scenes; nothing changes in how you use JonDash day to day. RESTARTS: an intentional restart - from Admin > Server, or the automatic restart after a module is installed, updated or removed - now brings everyone straight back into the dashboard still signed in, showing the familiar full-screen 'please wait' page while the server comes back. Shutting down stays the exception by design (it signs everyone out), and a crash or moving the install to another machine still signs everyone out too. SECURITY (from an independent review; access control itself was tested and found sound - the sign-in page could not be bypassed): signing in no longer reveals which email addresses have an account, because an unrecognised address used to fail faster and a locked account announced itself by name - every failed sign-in now does the same work and gives the same generic message, so a locked account just says the sign-in failed. Next.js and its bundled libraries were updated, clearing three high-severity advisories. The front page is never served from a build-time copy any more. A six-digit authenticator code can now only be used once, everywhere a code is asked for. Sessions now sign out after 2 hours of inactivity, which previously shipped switched off - THIS APPLIES TO EXISTING INSTALLS TOO, so set Idle timeout to 0 under Admin > Settings > Sessions if you would rather keep the old behaviour. And JonDash no longer advertises which framework it runs on.

A friendlier update and account experience, coming from 1.5.4 - nothing about your services or data changes. The 'updates available' notice is now a single compact banner coloured by how important the most urgent update is - green, amber or red - counting JonDash, modules and helpers together; click it to open the Updates page where the detail and controls live. The account buttons on every header collapse into one small account menu (My account and Sign out, with your email inside), which is far tidier on a phone and now reachable from the admin area too; signing out asks you to confirm first. Best of all, updating JonDash now KEEPS YOU SIGNED IN and lands on an 'Update successful' screen instead of bouncing you to the login page - a restart, or moving the install to another machine, still signs everyone out as before. The updating screen also reconnects as soon as the server is actually back.
