Module-system reliability fixes, coming from 1.5.3 — all about installing, building and testing add-ons; nothing changes for the base app or your services. A module's own styling no longer comes out half-applied (Tailwind skipped the folders installed modules live in, so a class only a module used could be missing and collapse its layout). A module database migration that fails part-way can now recover, because each file runs as one transaction that rolls back cleanly. A commented-out example line in a module is no longer read as a real declaration. A finished module install can no longer leave a marker that a later, unrelated build failure acts on to remove a healthy module. And there is now a supported way to test your own module against a database - `npm run test:modules` - working from a downloaded release or a git clone.

Beta: fixes `npm run test:modules` on a downloaded release (a follow-up to 1.5.4-beta.1). The module-test config ships in the download, but the two support files it needs lived in the tests folder, which is stripped from the download to keep it lean — so a module author testing their module against a downloaded release got a missing-file error. Those two files moved to a folder that ships. This only affects building and testing your own modules from a downloaded release; a git clone was always fine, and nothing about installing or running modules changes.

Beta: five fixes, all for installing or building modules. A module's own layout could come out half-styled - Tailwind skips the folders installed modules and helpers live in, so a class a module used that the base app did not was never generated (health monitoring's stat row collapsed from five columns to two); those classes are now generated. A module database migration that failed part-way could wedge forever - each migration file now runs as one transaction and rolls back cleanly, so a retry starts fresh. A commented-out example line in a module - a // helpers or // permissions - is no longer read as a real declaration, which could have installed a helper, rolled the module back, or overstated what you were asked to approve. A finished module install no longer leaves behind a marker that a later, unrelated build failure could use to remove a healthy module. And a module's own tests can now use a throwaway database. Nothing changes unless you install or build modules.

One page for everything that updates, and updates that can run on their own. Admin - Updates is now a single page in four parts: the version you are running, one Available updates list (Core, then Modules, then Helpers, each with a checkbox and the versions on offer), an Automatic updates master switch with a schedule and per-item exclusions, and the Beta channels switches. Automatic updates are new and off by default - when on, JonDash keeps itself, your modules and their helpers current on the schedule you set, but never applies a version that asks for more access than you approved, moves backwards, or would stop another module working, and it records what it held back. Backups can now be a single encrypted .dashbk file that also carries your service icons and each module's own data, so a restore or a move brings the whole instance back. Also: scheduled and background work is now recorded in the audit log as System, a downgrade is never offered as an update, encrypted backups no longer expose icons, an unreadable network config no longer falls back to the default port, and mail relays that authorise by IP are supported. Nothing changes unless you use these.

Beta: a helper that has been removed no longer appears under Updates. Uninstalling the last module that needed a helper removes that helper, but JonDash keeps a record of it so reinstalling the module brings its data back rather than starting from nothing. The Updates page was reading that record and still listing the helper - with a working beta switch and the ability to offer it updates - while the Helpers page correctly showed it as gone. Updates now goes by what is actually installed.

Beta: the beta switches for helpers now visibly work, and updating JonDash shows the updating screen again. The helper switches were writing the change correctly but the page kept showing the old value for up to three minutes, so they looked dead - the same fault was also making a channel change to JonDash itself, or to a module, appear to do nothing for the same window. All three now refresh immediately. Separately, updating JonDash stopped showing the full-screen 'updating' cover, so the page never reloaded onto the new version and sat there looking hung while the update had in fact finished; the cover is back.

Beta: fixes the beta switches for helpers, which did nothing. A helper normally follows the modules that need it, so one on beta only because a module is could not be switched off - the switch cleared the override, the channel was worked out again from the module still on beta, and it landed back where it started, redrawing unchanged. The switch now sets the channel you asked for, and only returns a helper to following its modules when you ask for the channel it would have chosen anyway. Rows also now say when a helper is pinned and no longer following.

Beta: a module's own settings page no longer shows its release channel and automatic-update state. Those controls moved to Admin - Updates a few releases ago, leaving the module page displaying copies it could not change - and the copies could fall out of step, so a module could read 'Currently on beta' while the switch for it on the Updates page was off. The page now carries a single line pointing at Admin - Updates, which cannot disagree with anything. Changing a module's channel also refreshes the Updates page properly, which it was missing before.

Beta: tidies up the Updates page. Several things had ended up in two places at once - notably two separate cards both titled Automatic updates, and an automatic-install tickbox that did the same job as the Automatic updates switch. The page is now four sections in the order you would work through them: which version you are running, what is available to update, whether it should update itself, and which beta channels you are on. The update schedule now sits inside the Automatic updates section and only appears once you turn the switch on, since it means nothing while it is off. Checking for updates and installing them now happen in one place instead of two.

Beta: one list of everything you can update. The separate Modules and Helpers update panels are replaced by a single Available updates list, grouped Core, then Modules, then Helpers. Each row has a checkbox and shows the name, the version you have and the one on offer, and how important the release is when the source says - JonDash's own releases do; module and helper manifests do not carry that yet, so nothing is shown for them rather than a made-up default. Tick what you want and press Update selected, or leave everything unticked and press Update all. JonDash's own update is applied on its own, because it restarts through the launcher rather than in-process, and running both from one click could leave an update half applied.

Beta: automatic updates are now one switch with exclusions. Turn Automatic updates on and JonDash, your modules and their helpers all stay current on your schedule; each one then gets its own switch to exclude it. It replaces the previous per-item opt-in, and is off by default - with it on, a module from any source you have added updates itself unless you exclude it. A helper excluded from automatic updates is still brought up to date when a module that needs it updates, since a module updated against a helper it cannot use is simply broken. Updates that ask for more access than you approved, are blocked, or would go backwards still wait for you.

Beta: the Helpers page is now about the helper, not its updates. The version line, beta-channel note and 'Pin to stable' button have moved to the Beta channels panel on Admin - Updates, which already lists every helper alongside JonDash and your modules. The Helpers page keeps what it is for: what each helper does, which modules use it, and what permission it implies - plus a Settings area reserved for helpers that offer settings. None do yet.

Beta: the Updates page no longer offers to move you BACKWARDS. A module or helper whose channel offers an older version than the one you have was being listed as an available update, with a tick-box beside it - so a single click could take you back to an earlier release. Anything older is now simply not offered. This shows up on the beta channel after a pre-release is promoted: a version like 0.0.5-beta.1 counts as older than 0.0.5, so once beta.1 becomes 0.0.5 the beta channel points at something older than what you are running until it is moved forward.

Beta: removes the duplicate update-channel selector. JonDash's channel now has a switch in the Beta channels panel alongside every module and helper, so the separate dropdown at the top of the Updates page was a second control for the same setting. That dropdown is gone; the panel above it still shows your installed version, update status and the automatic-install option, and now states which channel you are on with a pointer to the switch.

Beta: all beta-channel choices are now in one place. Admin - Updates has a new 'Beta channels' section that lists JonDash itself and every installed module and helper, each with a switch to opt in or out of pre-release versions. It stays collapsed when everything is on stable, and tells you how many things are on beta when they are not. The per-module channel control has been removed from each module's own page, which now just states which channel it is on and links here. A helper's channel normally follows the modules that need it; the switch pins it, and turning the switch off returns it to following rather than forcing it to stable.

Beta: an encrypted backup is now encrypted all the way through. Until now only the settings inside it were protected - every uploaded icon sat in the file as a plain image anyone could open without the passphrase, which for most people is a list of the services they run. Everything is now inside the encryption. Existing backups still restore, but they were affected, so replace any you are relying on. Backups also now include your module data - each module's configuration, stored records and dashboard layout - so restoring no longer leaves your modules installed but empty. The download is now a .dashbk file rather than a .zip; older .zip backups still restore. And if JonDash cannot read its network settings file it now says so and stops, instead of silently starting on plain HTTP port 3000 - which on an HTTPS install meant quietly serving unencrypted.

Beta: automatic updates actually work now, and everything that updates is on one page. The per-module 'update automatically' toggle shipped in v1.5.2 saved your choice and reported it as on, but nothing ever acted on it - no module was ever updated automatically. That is fixed, and helpers can now be opted in the same way. You choose when it runs: daily, weekly or monthly, at a time you pick, on a day of the week or day of the month. Admin - Updates is now the single page for all of it: JonDash itself and its channel, the schedule, and every module and helper with its version, channel and its own 'update automatically' tick - previously these were spread across four different screens. An update is still never applied automatically if it asks for more access than you approved, is blocked, goes backwards a version, or would stop another module working; those wait for you, and each run records what it held back and why.

Beta: the audit log now says when JonDash itself did something. Completing the previous release, work that runs on a schedule has no signed-in user, so it was leaving the User column empty - which reads as 'we don't know who did this' when the real answer is 'nothing did, it was the schedule'. In a security log those need telling apart. Scheduled entries are now marked System, and the User filter has a 'System (scheduled)' option so you can ask what ran overnight without anyone touching it. Existing entries are all recorded as user actions, which is accurate: before the previous release, scheduled work could not write to the audit log at all.

Beta: anything JonDash did on a schedule was missing from the audit log, silently. Only actions someone triggered by clicking were ever recorded - work that ran on a timer, such as a module tidying up old backups overnight or a health check, tried to save an entry, failed, and reported nothing. The log looked complete, so there was no reason to suspect the gap. Scheduled actions are now recorded like any other; they show no IP address, because no browser is involved, but the event itself is kept. Reported by the add-ons session after a module's first scheduled run.

Beta: JonDash can now send through a mail relay that authorises you by IP address instead of a sign-in - an internal smarthost, or Microsoft 365 direct send. Choose 'Mail relay (no authentication)' under Email; it connects without offering credentials and no longer insists on an account. There is also a new option to accept a relay's certificate when it isn't trusted, for an internal server using a private or self-signed one - off by default, limited to outgoing mail, recorded in the audit log, and shown in every test result so it can't be forgotten. Mail errors are much more useful too: every result now names the host, port and TLS mode it actually used - the test button uses your SAVED settings, so a failure no longer leaves you guessing whether it even tried the server on screen - and errors are explained rather than quoted, including untrusted, self-signed, expired and wrong-hostname certificates, a server that offers no authentication, a relay that refuses the recipient, and the common mistake of ticking 'Use TLS on connect' for a port that expects plain SMTP first.

Beta: a batch of fixes, several security-related. Moving or renaming the JonDash folder no longer breaks the install permanently - it rebuilds instead of failing on every page forever. Starting JonDash twice is refused rather than letting two copies fight over the same database. Two ways a module could reach the network or the filesystem without declaring it have been closed - filesystem access is meant to be refused to modules outright, so that one mattered most. Send test email no longer hangs forever: it fails within seconds, says which step failed, and names the usual causes including that Microsoft 365 disables SMTP AUTH per mailbox by default. Full-screen updating and restarting messages cover the whole screen again instead of just the middle column. The module import button is always visible rather than appearing only after you pick a file. And the audit log now records which setting changed and its new value, with encrypted settings recorded as hidden.

Add-ons stay up to date, and you can see what they are allowed to do. A new Update everything button updates every module and helper waiting, in one restart, skipping anything that needs a decision from you and saying what it skipped. Modules gain a per-module automatic update switch, off by default - a version asking for more access than you approved is never applied automatically either way. Fixes a real gap: a module could gain a capability you were never shown, because a helper's declaration of what it can do was being silently discarded. What you approve now includes everything the module's helpers can do, highlighted as high-risk. Helpers can also be updated at all for the first time - previously a helper only changed version as a side effect of a module install, so a helper could publish a security fix no existing install would ever receive - and a shared helper no longer flip-flops between versions. Nothing changes if you do not install modules.

Beta: keeping add-ons up to date. A new Update everything button updates every module and helper with something waiting in one restart, skipping anything that needs a decision from you and saying what it skipped. Modules gain a per-module automatic update switch, off by default and deliberately not one setting for everything - a version asking for more access than you approved is never applied automatically either way. Helpers now appear on the Updates page and can be updated at all: previously a helper only changed version as a side effect of a module install, so a helper could publish a security fix no existing install would ever receive. A shared helper no longer flip-flops between versions depending on which module you touched last, and a helper that has to break compatibility names the modules it will stop working before it is installed. Nothing changes if you do not install modules.

Beta: a module's helpers now appear on the screen where you approve it. Helpers can do things modules are forbidden - reading and writing your files, for example - and a helper is meant to declare that so JonDash can tell you before you install anything using it. That declaration was being silently discarded, so a module could take a helper with access to your files while the approval screen listed only its own milder permissions. What you approve now includes everything the module's helpers can do, whether or not the module named it, and those entries are highlighted as high-risk. A capability JonDash cannot make sense of is refused outright rather than dropped. Helpers now supply their own wording, so the screen can say what actually happens to your machine. Nothing changes if you do not install modules, and no module you already have behaves differently.

Keeping modules up to date, and modules that can work in the background. Module updates now live in Admin -> Updates alongside JonDash's own - each module shows its installed and available version, you can update several together in one restart, and everything they have stored is kept. Modules are never updated automatically, even when JonDash updates itself, and a version wanting more access than you approved must be approved first. Modules can also now declare background work that runs from the moment JonDash starts rather than when someone opens a page, so a monitoring module restarted overnight keeps watching. This is delivered by helpers: shared components that come only from the official add-ons source, arrive with the module that needs them, and are listed read-only under Admin -> Helpers. Modules from the official source repair themselves if something they need goes missing; ones you imported or got elsewhere are reported instead. Nothing restarts on its own. Nothing changes if you do not install modules.

Beta: JonDash now notices when a module is missing something it needs. A module can end up installed but quietly doing nothing if the shared component it relies on is not there - which could happen to anything installed during earlier 1.5.0 betas. Admin -> Modules now checks, and for modules from the official add-ons source it downloads what is missing automatically and offers you a Restart now button to finish the job. Modules you imported yourself, or installed from another source, are reported rather than repaired - JonDash will not fetch code on their behalf without you asking. Nothing restarts on its own.

Beta fixes for importing your own module. A failed import left the module's files behind: you were told it had failed, but it was quietly compiled in on the next restart without the helper it needed, so its background work never ran. A module that cannot have the helper it declares is now refused outright rather than installed in a state where it can never work - and installing from a source behaves the same way, which it previously did not. Importing also looked for helpers on the stable channel only, so importing a module needing a beta-only helper always failed; it now follows your own update channel.

Beta fixes from a full module lifecycle test. Helpers never actually installed with the module that needed them, and were never removed when nothing needed them any more - so the whole helper mechanism did nothing, silently. Importing a module or updating one never installed helpers either. Also fixed: a brand-new install showed an empty module browser instead of setting up the official source, you had to enable a module (approving every permission it asks for) before you could uninstall one you had decided against, the Helpers page was missing from the sidebar, and installing a module now tells you if a helper comes with it.

Beta: helpers are now installed from the official add-ons source alongside the module that needs them, rather than shipping inside JonDash. A module declares the helpers it requires and they arrive with it in the same batch and the same restart; when nothing needs a helper any more its files are removed, but its data is kept, so reinstalling brings it back intact. Helpers can only ever come from the official source - that is enforced, not assumed, because a helper is trusted to do things modules are deliberately forbidden. Admin -> Helpers still lists what is installed and which modules rely on it.

Beta: groundwork for modules that can do more. Modules can now declare background work that runs from the moment JonDash starts, rather than only when someone opens a page - so a monitoring module restarted overnight actually keeps watching. This is delivered by a new kind of built-in component called a helper: shared capability that comes with JonDash, is used only when a module asks for it, and is listed read-only under Admin -> Helpers so you can see what is on your system and why. Helpers exist so that modules can eventually do things they are deliberately forbidden from doing directly - reaching the filesystem, for example - through a narrow, purpose-built interface you approve, rather than by trusting the module itself. Nothing changes if you have no modules installed.

Beta: module updates now live in Admin -> Updates, in their own section under JonDash's update panel - installed and available versions, which channel each module follows, and where it came from. Select several and update them together: one rebuild and one restart, and their data is kept. You are told when module updates are waiting, wherever JonDash already flags an update, even when JonDash itself is up to date. Modules are NEVER updated automatically, not even when JonDash auto-installs its own updates - updating a module is always your choice. And a version wanting more access than you approved says so in plain language and needs your approval first. Also fixes two problems that made updating unsafe: a module that added a new table or column in a later version ran against the old layout with no error, and an updated module kept the permissions recorded when it was first enabled, so new capabilities it declared quietly did not work.

Modules: JonDash can now be extended with add-ons that plug in without changing the base app. Admin -> Settings -> Modules lets you browse the official add-ons source (or any public GitHub repo that publishes modules), install several at once, or import your own .zip. Before anything installs you see in plain language exactly what it can do, and a module is refused if its code reaches for something it did not declare - a strong safety net, though not a sandbox, so only install modules you trust. If a module ever stops JonDash building, it is removed automatically and you are told which one. Modules can add a dashboard widget, their own pages and settings, background checks and email. You choose who sees each module using Service Groups, and each person can resize and arrange their own widgets. Nothing changes if you install no modules.

Beta: three module-framework fixes found while testing for the 1.4.0 stable release. A module's own settings screen never appeared - the framework silently ignored it - and now renders under Admin -> Modules -> the module, below its simple settings. Modules can no longer request permissions that do nothing: nine of thirteen were never connected to anything, including "Create, modify or delete your user accounts", which looked alarming at approval time and granted nothing; only outbound connections, encryption, audit entries and sending email remain, and the others return when they are actually built. And legitimate modules are no longer rejected over ordinary English - the check that blocks dynamically loaded code was matching plain wording like "Bulk import (JSON)" on a module's own page. No published module is affected.

Beta fix: installing, importing or uninstalling a module no longer leaves the page stuck on "Installing…". Because a module is built into the dashboard, those actions rebuild and restart JonDash - and the page that triggered them was left waiting forever with no explanation. You now get the same full-screen "Applying your module changes…" cover used for updates and restarts, which waits for the new server and returns you to sign-in on its own. If a restart never actually starts, it now says so and offers a reload instead of spinning indefinitely.

Beta: uninstall several modules at once. Each installed module now has a tick box - select the ones you want gone and remove them together, so you get one rebuild and one restart for the whole batch instead of one per module, and the confirmation names every module being deleted first. This completes the bulk selection added in 1.4.0-beta.5, which only covered installing.

Beta fix: Browse modules crashed whenever a channel actually had modules to show. Admin -> Modules -> Browse modules gave an error page instead of the list, so nothing could be installed from a source. It only happened once a channel had something published in it, which is why the empty stable channel looked fine while beta failed. Selecting and installing modules works normally again.

Critical fix - install this. Since 1.4.0-beta.3, updating could leave JonDash unable to start. The rule protecting your installed add-ons from being overwritten matched any folder named 'modules' anywhere in the app, including the module framework itself, so updates stopped copying it - and if an update then failed, the automatic rollback deleted it without being able to put it back. The rule now only matches top-level folders. Your data was never at risk. If your install is already stuck and won't start, a normal update cannot fix it (the faulty updater is the thing doing the updating) - see 'Recovering an install that won't start' in CHANGELOG.md for the one-time manual step.

DO NOT USE THIS VERSION - it can leave JonDash unable to start. A fault in this build (present in 1.4.0-beta.3 through 1.4.0-beta.6) means updating can delete part of the app itself, and if that update then fails the automatic rollback cannot put it back, so the app will not start and cannot repair itself. Install 1.4.0-beta.7 or later instead. Your data is not at risk. If you are already stuck, see "Recovering an install that won't start" in CHANGELOG.md - a normal update cannot fix it. Original notes: Beta: control who sees each module, and arrange your own dashboard. A module can now be limited to Service Groups just like a service tile (Admin -> Modules -> the module -> 'Who can see this module') - leave every group unticked and everyone signed in sees it, tick some and only their members do; its page returns not-found to anyone else. Each module widget also gains a Customise control to set its width and height and move it around, and your layout is yours alone - it never changes what anyone else sees. Modules can ship their own icon, and can now offer multiline settings for things like a JSON configuration. The authoring guide explains how to design a widget that users resize.

Browse modules now has a checkbox on each module - tick the ones you want and install them together, so you get one rebuild and one restart for the whole batch instead of one per module. And you're now warned before anything restarts: installing, importing or uninstalling a module shows a confirmation first, explaining that JonDash will rebuild and restart and that everyone signed in will be signed out. Nothing restarts until you confirm. The module-authoring guide's AI prompt has also been updated - it described the framework as it was before modules could perform actions, so modules generated from it would have been rejected at install.

Install 1.4.0-beta.7 or later instead. Your data is not at risk. If you are already stuck, see "Recovering an install that won't start" in CHANGELOG.md - a normal update cannot fix it. Original notes: Beta fix - install this if you have installed any module. JonDash recorded every module as though it shipped with the app, which defeated the safeguard protecting installed modules: if a module ever failed to load, its tables, settings and stored data could be wiped automatically (for a health monitor, that means every monitor and all of its history). JonDash now records where each module came from, repairs existing records itself, and never removes a module whose files are still there. Also: a module installed from the beta channel is now correctly marked as beta, so its per-module update channel is right; and Browse modules explains that a just-published module can take a couple of minutes to appear.

DO NOT USE THIS VERSION - it can leave JonDash unable to start. A fault in this build (present in 1.4.0-beta.3 through 1.4.0-beta.6) means updating can delete part of the app itself, and if that update then fails the automatic rollback cannot put it back, so the app will not start and cannot repair itself. Install 1.4.0-beta.7 or later instead. Your data is not at risk. If you are already stuck, see "Recovering an install that won't start" in CHANGELOG.md - a normal update cannot fix it. Original notes: Beta: modules can now be installed for real. Admin -> Settings -> Modules -> Browse modules installs a module from a source, or import your own as a .zip; JonDash checks the module first (refusing anything that uses a capability it didn't declare, touches the filesystem, runs constructed code or reaches into app internals), then rebuilds and restarts so it's live - so you'll need to sign in again. If a module ever stops the app building, JonDash removes it, starts up without it and tells you. Modules can now also have working buttons, send email and ping hosts. Uninstalling now removes a module completely, and each module shows whether it's Enabled, Disabled or Not set up. The bundled Sample module has been removed.

Beta: modules can now come from a source repository. Admin -> Settings -> Modules gains 'Manage sources' (add any public GitHub repo that publishes modules; the official add-ons source is set up for you) and 'Browse modules', showing what each source publishes per stable/beta channel along with the permissions each module requests. Each module also gets its own 'opt into beta releases' toggle, separate from JonDash's update channel. Installing from a source arrives in the next update.

Beta: new Modules system (early foundation). Admin -> Settings -> Modules lets you enable, configure and remove optional add-ons that plug in without changing the base app; each module shows the permissions it needs before you enable it, and a bundled Sample module (a dashboard widget + its own page) demonstrates it. Installing modules from a repository or importing your own comes in a later update. Build your own with the guide + paste-in AI prompt in docs/MODULES-AUTHORING.md.

Beta: full server backup — one file now captures your entire server (accounts, service groups, access roles, all settings, network/HTTPS config, icons, and the encryption key when you set a passphrase), and restore lets you choose what to bring back. Fixes the bug where your authenticator (2FA) stopped working after a restore: an encrypted backup now carries the key across, so 2FA survives a restore or migration. Encrypted backups now require a strong passphrase.

Beta: applying an update or restarting now shows a full-screen 'Updating…' screen that waits for the server to be reliably back before returning you to sign-in, so a too-quick refresh no longer briefly breaks remote access. New Restart & Shut down controls under Admin -> Settings -> Server power (full-admin only). And an update/restart now signs you out fully — login starts at the password step, not a leftover 2-factor prompt — so you can sign in as a different account.

Beta: small robustness fix — the server now clears its 'update in progress' rollback marker once it has booted successfully, instead of only on a later crash, so a much-later unrelated crash can't wrongly roll back a version that's working fine.

Beta fixes for 1.3.5-beta.1: the server no longer restart-loops (and signs you out repeatedly) when the OS/console stops it — it now stops cleanly; self-updating no longer corrupts the launcher script mid-write; and a harmless session-cleanup error no longer shows in the console.

Beta: the launcher now supervises the server — it captures crashes to a log and auto-restarts, and gives up cleanly instead of leaving it down. Updates are safer too: JonDash snapshots itself before updating and automatically rolls back to the previous version if an update fails to start, with an on-screen notice. New 'automatically install updates' checkbox (off by default) under Admin -> Updates. Your data, settings and uploads are never touched by an update or rollback.

Beta: access roles now cover the whole admin area. Two new delegable capabilities — Manage network & HTTPS and Manage email — let you grant those areas to a user via an access role instead of full-admin-only, and the settings capability now also covers Updates. Full admins are unaffected and existing access roles keep exactly the powers they had.

Beta: the admin menu is reorganised into a left 'Settings' sidebar (General, Server settings, Security), with Updates on its own page. Plus fixes: Off-mode network save works, the update-channel toggle updates immediately, 'Update now' returns to the sign-in screen after restarting, and the mobile service-edit form no longer runs off-screen.

Beta: better mobile support — on small screens the header no longer crowds or scrolls sideways (the version tag and long labels collapse) and spacing is tighter. Desktop is unchanged. Groundwork; the bigger mobile improvement comes with the admin 'Settings' redesign.

Beta: smoother page transitions — the page content now fades in gently as you move between pages, while the header and navigation stay put. Automatically disabled if your system prefers reduced motion.

Update channels: choose Stable or Beta under Admin -> Settings -> Updates, with a Check-for-updates button. Plus you can now restore a backup on the first-run setup screen to migrate an install from another machine.

Outgoing email support: connect an SMTP account (Gmail, Outlook/Hotmail, Microsoft 365, or custom) with an app password, or via OAuth2 for Google and Microsoft, and send a test email — set up under Admin -> Email. Nothing sends automatically yet; it's the groundwork for emailed setup links and password reset.

Bug fixes: backups are now a compressed archive that actually includes your icon images (and older .json backups still restore), and uploading or restoring files over 1 MB no longer causes an error page.

Optional HTTPS: get an automatic Let's Encrypt certificate (or use your own) and pick the ports, under Admin -> Network & HTTPS. Off by default. The launcher now self-heals a failed update by rebuilding from clean, and keeps a local, redacted diagnostics log.
Removes a harmless startup warning about an unsupported config option. No functional change.
Fixes a build failure when updating an already-shrunk install — the per-machine build no longer re-runs type-checking that needs files the size-optimisation removes.
Restarting the server now signs everyone out: active sessions are invalidated on restart, so a taken or lingering session can't outlive a restart.
Even smaller install: after building, files never used at runtime (type definitions, sourcemaps, build cache) are removed too — about 26,000 files down to ~9,000.
Fixes sign-in and two-factor errors introduced by the 1.1.5 self-contained build. Restores the proven, smaller-install approach from 1.1.4.
Much smaller install: build-only packages are pruned after each build (~40% fewer files). The app now rebuilds only when the version changes.
Delegated admin permissions: grant specific admin powers to a user via Access Roles without full admin. Session and audit-log settings moved to their own pages.
Adds an internal automated test and CI suite. Developer-only — no changes to the app you run.
Shows the installed version in the admin header. Confirms auto-update is working.
Credential-free auto-update from the public repo, showing each update's type and priority.
Fixes broken styling when the dashboard is opened over a LAN IP address.
Adds Settings, Audit log, and account self-service; renames Roles to Service Groups.
Adds two-factor backup codes, the session manager, and backup & restore.
Initial release.
